messages:
emily: FYI we enabled strict fncall validation on canary-eu at 09:10 and rejects spiked to ~5.6% (baseline ~0.5%). not sure this is input drift.

rick: can you paste the top reject examples + panel link? are these validator rejects or routing->degen fallbacks?

emily: panel: https://console.redwood.internal/d/validators/eu?panel=fncall_rejects (slice=canary). metric is validator.rejects and fallback->degen_count increased. example from trace sample: 
```json
{"tool_response": ["ok"], "validation_error": "expected object for tool_response, got array"}
```

anand: seems like some adapters return arrays instead of the required object. question: how are rejects attributed in telemetry & billing — original route or final routed tag?

ops-bot: Canary 'strict-validate-canary-eu' auto-paused: reject_rate > 2.5% for 3/5 mins.

emily: asks before unpause: (1) add reject_reason histogram with human labels in the rollout panel + link to sampled traces for top buckets, (2) make billing attribution explicit in rollout UI (are rejects billable?).

rick: logs currently emit validator.code. UI needs canonical labels (e.g. TOOL_SHAPE_ARRAY_INSTEAD_OF_OBJ). sample rate for reject traces is 1/100; propose 1/10 for canary for 1 hour.

anand: infra plan: add a normalizer that maps common adapter mismatches to stable reject_reason strings behind a feature flag; emit original_route_id + final_route_tag in validation logs to disambiguate. also add header X-Validate-Sample to force trace sampling.

billing: tagging billing ops — we need a short policy doc: how do we count rejects for usage? (billable request vs zero-cost diagnostic).

emily: filing PLAT-3610: "canary-eu strict-validate follow-up: reject_reason histogram + trace links + billing attribution". assign @rick @anand @billing. do not unpause until histogram + trace links + explicit billing flag are present. sync in 15m in #eng-platform. :thumbsup:
